title: Compatibility of the Tate twists
statement:
For every $m\in\mathbf Z$, the functorial pullback of roots of unity
gives a strict arrow
$\Phi_X^*E(1)\stackrel{\sim}{\to}E(1)$, and the Tate twist functor
$(-)(m)$ of [def-wf-tate-twist] commutes with finite scalar
extension.

proof.text: Use the finite-field datum, $X_0$, $X$, the automorphism $\Phi_X$, and the raw rational coefficient categories of [def-wf-weil-category]. Put $R_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $L_E=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_X\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_X}(\mathcal O_E)_X$. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], $L_E$ is a locally free rank-one $R_E$-module with its stated finite reductions. Let $L_E^{[m]}$ denote its signed tensor powers: unit for $m=0$, left-associated tensor powers for $m>0$, sheaf dual of the positive power for $m<0$. Locally these are all $R_E$. The characterization [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] applies: $X$ is noetherian and finite-dimensional, being of finite type over $k$, and $\ell$ is invertible. Thus each signed line is an object of the PBC integral category, using the single stratum $X$ and perfect model $\mathcal O_E[0]$. Tensoring any stratified perfect model for $K$ with such a line leaves that model unchanged on a refining cover, so it preserves this category. The same characterization identifies this category with the completed integral category in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] over this $X$. Consequently its signed-line rationalizations are the $E(m)$ of [def-wf-tate-twist]; tensor with a line needs no additional completion, since the resulting object is already complete. This identifies the conventions here without replacing the rational category by discrete $E$-module sheaves.

source.place: Proof, opening formula; explicit completed integral representatives

proof.text: Apply clauses 1--3 of [lem-pur-integral-twist-line-inverse-image] with $h=\Phi_X$ and $H=E$. They give the coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_{\Phi,E}:\Phi_X^{-1}R_E\cong R_E$, the root-limit isomorphism $\tau:\Phi_X^{-1}\mathbf Z_\ell(1)\cong\mathbf Z_\ell(1)$, and the semilinear isomorphism $\rho_E:\Phi_X^{-1}L_E\cong L_E$. Its $r$th root projection is the pulled-back root projection followed by the canonical roots-of-unity map; in particular the maps commute with $u\mapsto u^\ell$. Here $\Phi_X$ is a scheme automorphism, so [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] ensures that its inverse image really preserves the inverse limit. With the coefficient map $\alpha_{\Phi,E}$, $\rho_E$ is a linear isomorphism $P_E L_E\to L_E$. The transport $P_E$ is precisely the integral transport underlying the rationalized $\Phi_X^*$ of [def-wf-weil-category]. Rationalizing gives $\tau_{E,1}:\Phi_X^*E(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}E(1)$, the claimed strict Weil datum. No claim that inverse image along an arbitrary morphism preserves arbitrary limits is used.

source.place: Proof, canonical root pullbacks and their inverse limit

proof.text: For $m=0$ use the coefficient-unit comparison. For $m>0$ tensor the datum of step 2 in the left-associated order fixed by [def-wf-tate-twist], inserting the tensor-pullback comparison. For $m<0$ apply internal Hom to the positive power and the unit. The statements [lem-wf-tensor-weil] and [lem-wf-internal-hom-weil] give these Weil objects and their maps: the latter specifies $H(\varphi_K^{-1},\varphi_L)\alpha_{K,L}$, with the first argument contravariant. On integral lines apply [lem-pur-signed-line-derived-base-change] to the ringed-site equivalence $\Phi_X$ with coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_{\Phi,E}$ and line isomorphism $\rho_E$. The sites use the fixed small-site universe, the equivalence preserves finite limits and coverings, and step 1 gives locally free lines. Rebracket its right-associated powers to the left-associated powers here using canonical tensor associators: on a local line basis both identify the same ordered tensor of $m$ generators, and their dual maps identify its dual generator. A change of basis multiplies both positive generators by $u^m$ and both dual generators by $u^{-m}$, so these identifications agree on overlaps and commute with transport. The negative datum is characterized by preservation of evaluation, equivalently $\mathcal Hom(\rho_{E,m}^{-1},\alpha_{\Phi,E})$ after the internal-Hom comparison. Thus these are precisely the signed Weil maps of [def-wf-tate-twist]. Only the asserted bifunctors and conjugation are used; no triangulation of fixed pairs is required.

source.place: Proof, tensor products for positive exponents and internal Homs for negative exponents

proof.text: Fix finite intermediate fields $E\subset F$. There is a canonical map $b_{FE}:L_E\otimes_{R_E}R_F\to L_F$ induced by $t\otimes a\mapsto t\otimes a$ on the coefficient inclusions. To check it is an isomorphism, use the compatible-root cover in [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. On that cover $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)$ has basis $e$ over $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_\ell$, and the same node identifies $R_H=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_\ell\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_X}(\mathcal O_H)_X$ for $H=E,F$. Hence $b_{FE}$ is the multiplication isomorphism $R_E\otimes_{R_E}R_F\to R_F$ in these coordinates. Its inverse is $s\mapsto1\otimes s$. These formulas are unchanged by replacing $e$ by $ue$ for a unit $u$, so give the canonical isomorphism globally. For $E\subset F\subset H$ the two composite maps agree, since both send $(e\otimes a)\otimes b\otimes c$ to $e\otimes abc$; for repeated fields this is the unitor.

source.place: Proof, finite scalar extension: degree-one comparison by balanced tensors

proof.text: By [lem-sp-invertible-tensor-scalar-extension], $b_{FE}$ extends to canonical isomorphisms $b_{FE,m}:L_E^{[m]}\otimes_{R_E}R_F\cong L_F^{[m]}$ for every integer $m$, compatible with units, powers, duals and successive extensions. The integral functor underlying the transition $T_{F/E}$ of [def-wf-weil-category] is the ordinary derived change of rings $B_{FE}K=K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_F$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] (its $C_{F/E}$), restricted to constructible objects and rationalized, with $T_{E/E}=\mathrm{id}$ literally. Apply [lem-pur-completed-line-tensor-coherence] to a field chain with these $R_E,L_E,b_{FE}$; its hypotheses are exactly the line, unit and composition checks in steps 1 and 4. It gives natural isomorphisms $\bar\beta_{FE,m,K}:B_{FE}(K\otimes^L_{R_E}L_E^{[m]})\cong B_{FE}K\otimes^L_{R_F}L_F^{[m]}$, on a flat-term K-flat representative $(x\otimes l)\otimes s\mapsto(x\otimes s)\otimes b_{FE,m}(l\otimes1)$. This $\bar\beta$, for the functor $B_{FE}$ actually used by the Weil transition, is the comparison of this proof; its conjugate $\beta$ by the maps $\chi$ of that node is the same comparison for the quotient-tower extension $C_{FE}$ and is not needed. The same node states that each $T_{i,m}$ preserves derived completeness, so for complete $K$ the completion maps of the completed tensor of [def-wf-tensor-product] are isomorphisms $K\otimes^L L^{[m]}\cong K\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}^L L^{[m]}$; by step 1 these rationalize to $K(m)$, and both sides of $\bar\beta$ lie in the constructible categories. For $E=F$, $\bar\beta_{EE,m}$ followed by the multiplication isomorphisms $K\otimes_{R_E}R_E\cong K$ is the identity on pure tensors, matching $T_{E/E}=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Proof, finite scalar extension: signed powers and the ordinary derived scalar extension of the Weil transition

proof.text: The integral functors $B_{FE}T_{E,m}$ and $T_{F,m}B_{FE}$ are additive and semilinear over $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_F$. By [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization], the integral comparisons $\bar\beta$ of step 5, composed with the completion isomorphisms there, give natural isomorphisms $\beta_{FE,m,K}:T_{F/E}(K(m))\xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{F/E}K)(m)$ in the raw rational categories. Its inverted-element condition holds: the image of $\varpi_E\ne0$ is invertible in $F=\mathcal O_F[1/\varpi_F]$. On a localized arrow $f/\varpi_E^r$ the extension is $T(f)/\varpi_E^r$, so the integral naturality equation, multiplied by this same denominator on both sides, is precisely rational naturality. The finite-extension and pullback comparisons here are those of [def-wf-weil-category]; its transition on Weil pairs is $(K,\varphi_K)\mapsto(TK,T(\varphi_K)\circ c_K)$, where $c:P_FT\cong TP_E$. It remains to check that $\beta$ commutes with these data; an underlying natural isomorphism alone would not finish the claim.

source.place: Proof, finite scalar extension: rationalization and the required Weil morphism equation

proof.text: Clause 4 of [lem-pur-integral-twist-line-inverse-image] gives $\rho_F\Phi_X^{-1}(j_{EF})=j_{EF}\rho_E$ as well as the corresponding coefficient-ring equation. Balancing this equality with $R_F$ says exactly that $b_{FE,1}$ intertwines the degree-one Frobenius data with the scalar/pullback comparison. The signed-line naturality clause of [lem-pur-signed-line-derived-base-change] extends this square to $b_{FE,m}$ for every integer $m$. For negative $m$ it follows by the evaluation equation in that statement: compose either proposed square with evaluation and the already equal positive-power square; both become the coefficient-unit square, and the perfect evaluation of a line determines its dual map uniquely. Thus there is no use of scalar extension commuting with an arbitrary internal Hom.

source.place: Proof, naturality: the explicit Frobenius square on signed lines

proof.text: The ordinary binary tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], for the identity geometric morphism and coefficient map $R_E\to R_F$, followed by $1\otimes b_{FE,m}$, is the $\bar\beta$ of step 5. Its compatibility with the transport comparison of [def-wf-automorphism-completed-transport] can be checked on flat-term K-flat representatives: both routes send $(x\otimes l)\otimes s$ to $(\Phi x\otimes\Phi s)\otimes\rho_{F,m}(\Phi b_{FE,m}(l\otimes1))$, with the equality supplied by step 7. These are equal maps of total tensor complexes, since all factors other than $x$ are in degree zero. The twist uses the completed tensor of [def-wf-tensor-product], whose completion maps are isomorphisms here (step 5). Its transport comparison $\mu$ is built by applying the inverse-image equivalence componentwise to the product and mapping-fiber terms of the Koszul completion model. Transport is an exact equivalence preserving products [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], and its coefficient map fixes $\varpi$; so it carries each tower projection, each transition and $1-t$ to the same maps, and carries the completion map, with zero shifted-product component, to the completion map. The just-checked ordinary square consequently commutes also after composing with the completion isomorphisms on both sides. This checks the comparison for the actual completed twist rather than inferring it from equality of all derived reductions.

source.place: Proof, naturality: binary tensor and completed-twist square

proof.text: Finally tensor the equal square of step 8 with the datum $\varphi_K$ of a Weil object. Bifunctor naturality and the definition of the tensor datum give $\beta_K\circ\varphi_{T(K(m))}=\varphi_{(TK)(m)}\circ P_F(\beta_K)$. After rationalization this remains an equality by [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization]. By the morphism definition in [def-wf-weil-category], $\beta_K$ is therefore an isomorphism of strict Weil pairs, natural in $K$. The unit, positive-power and negative-evaluation normalizations of steps 3 and 5 identify these with the twists of [def-wf-tate-twist]. This proves that $(-)(m)$ commutes with finite scalar extension for all $m$, including $0$ and negative integers, together with the roots-of-unity arrow of step 2.

source.place: Proof, final naturality assertion: conclude in the category of strict pairs
